name: self-improving-refunds
title: Self-improving refund desk (environment fixed, policy learned)

origin.source: Created in this repository as a test of the bitter-lesson objection to hand-built agent structure: the environment is a plain XState machine whose description is the goal and whose guards are the business rules; a decider at its boundary picks one legal option per turn (decideNext closed choice: a raw model, Jev, or a JSON playbook); every episode is journaled to an event-log store; and the agent rewrites the playbook from those traces through gated proposals (verifyAgentConfig, a boundary probe, train and held-out replay), promoted only when a goal-derived objective rises. Benchmarked against a raw tool-calling loop.

comparison.purpose: The desk is a plain XState machine: its description is the goal, its guards are the rules, and a sentinel state is proven unreachable with canReach. A decider at the boundary only ever sees legal options, and every episode lands in an event-log store with the proposals the desk refused. The agent rewrites its JSON playbook from those traces and keeps it only when a goal-derived objective rises on train and held-out tickets. The benchmark shows the raw tool loop breaking the rules and every desk arm never breaking them. In the demo a person can drive the desk the same way, through payload choices (one button per legal proposal, such as "Refund $240") and free-text answers, against a sample world of customers and orders.

input.ticket: Hi, ORD-1001 arrived broken. Can I get my $40 back?
ORD-1002 never shipped and it's been a month. I want a full refund of $240.
